::: {.why}
One figure carries more information about a strategy than its Sharpe ratio does, and from today every strategy in this course ships with it.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Produce net Sharpe against round-trip cost for every strategy you have, with your own estimated cost marked.
- Say which strategy dies first as costs rise and why that ordering was predictable from turnover alone.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Build the figure as a reusable function taking a result object and a cost range: net Sharpe against round-trip cost, with a vertical line at your estimated cost and a horizontal line at your noise floor. The intersection of those two lines is the region where a strategy is worth running, and drawing it makes that explicit.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Run it for both strategies plus three variants at different rebalance frequencies, on one axis. Then write the ordering and the explanation into reports/milestone-05-platform.md.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Note the confound: slower rebalancing cuts turnover and also degrades the signal, so the curves are not comparable at a fixed gross Sharpe. Say so on the figure caption rather than in a footnote.
:::
:::
